Subject: Nimbus Health — scale qualification & action plan

Hi Kevin / Siobhan —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps for technical qualification around SLOs and burst capacity. I pulled this together so we have a single place to align before the load test.

Key SLO targets you asked for (from the call):
- Steady-state p95 latency ≤ 250 ms (generation end-to-end)
- Burst concurrency target: sustain 1,200 concurrent requests for short windows (2-5 minutes)
- Sustained throughput target: 150 requests/sec for peak API paths
- Streaming clients: token-stream latency per token target ≤ 80 ms and first-byte latency under 200 ms

Observability and failover requirements we noted:
- Track p50/p95/p99, token-level emit times, KV cache hit rate, and queue length metrics
- Fallback policy: automatic route to smaller model variant (quantized) after 10s queueing or on degraded latency

Proposed qualification plan (high level):
1) Pre-test checklist (this week): identify a representative prompt set, share auth/API keys for the dedicated test project, and confirm test account ACLs. (Owner: Kevin + Marcus)
2) Baseline run (day 1): 30-min steady-state at nominal concurrency to collect p95 distribution and token counts. (Owner: Jasmine)
3) Burst test (day 2): scripted ramp to 3x baseline concurrency with short holds (2/5/10-min windows), validate warm-pool effectiveness and cold-start times. Target: observe scale-up < 30s for prewarmed instances, queueing < 10s before fallback. (Owner: Jasmine)
4) Streaming test (parallel): client-side stream test with 100 concurrent streams for 10 min, verify token latency and first-byte metrics. (Owner: Lauren + Jasmine)
5) Post-test review: map telemetry to SLO gates and recommend config (batching, cache TTLs, warm pool sizing). (Owner: Marcus)

I attached a simple scale matrix and a draft MAP (mutual action plan) for procurement + SOC2 evidence items. Please review and let me know any changes to priorities / dates.

Next steps we suggest today: confirm test window (we proposed Wed 2/25 AM PT), share representative prompt set and a sample user-identity footprint (token lengths, streaming vs non).

Thanks —

Hi Kevin —

Quick answers and what I'll validate during the run:

1) Concurrency definition: we measure concurrent in-flight model generations (i.e., generation calls that occupy a model slot). For your scenario, average 3.2s per request would map to required model slots = RPS * avg_latency. For your target of 150 RPS, that implies baseline concurrency ~480 slots; the 1,200 number is the Burst concurrency we aim to sustain during short windows. I'll provide an exact mapping sheet in the matrix.

2) Warm pool semantics: Redwood supports both prewarmed reserved slots (billed as reserved capacity) and opportunistic warm instances from autoscaler. For the qualification test we can enable a temporary prewarm pool (non-billed demo mode) so you can see warm-start behavior. By default in hosted mode, idle instances are kept warm for ~90s before scaling down; with dedicated/reserved pool you can set longer TTLs. Prewarm spin-up observed in our staging tests: first usable token from a cold instance ~6-12s depending on model & quantization; prewarmed slot reuse is effectively immediate. We'll measure in your environment during the baseline.

3) Fallback and quality gate: we recommend a two-tier policy: automatic fallback to a quantized variant only after queue timeout (10s) AND quality regression detector. The detector runs a small prompt set (3-5 golden prompts) and compares embeddings + scoring; if quality drops > 6% on the metric we will failback to the larger model. We'll run the regression step between ramp phases.

Planned telemetry to capture (I'll instrument these): p50/p95/p99 generation latency, model slot utilization, queue length, KV cache hit ratio, memory pressure, first-byte token delay, client RTT. I'll share the small test harness and k6 scripts.

I'll lead the baseline + burst test. Please place the API key in the shared secret vault I sent via separate email and confirm test IP allowlist (Kevin).

-Jasmine
